transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Thank you so much. Um, well, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. It's probably just me being a bit silly, but... I've been feeling, I guess, a little restless lately? 

I just feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. Even when I'm completely worn out and I know I really should just be sitting still, I get this feeling like I have to jump up and do the next thing. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you recently started or changed any medications?

Oh, no, I haven't. Um, I haven't started anything new or changed anything at all. I try to be very careful about all that, you know? I haven't even added a new vitamin or anything over-the-counter. I hope that's okay... I just always want to make sure I'm doing the right thing before I put anything in my body. Did I answer that right, or did you mean something else?
Aside from feeling restless, do you find yourself constantly worrying about a lot of different everyday things?

Oh, gosh, no, I don't think so. I try very hard to be a positive person, you know? I wouldn't want you to think I'm just a worrywart who sits around fretting over every little everyday thing. 

I mean, I think I worry a normal amount, like anyone else would, but it's definitely not constant. I really try to just take things as they come so I don't bother anyone with my problems. It's really just that physical feeling of needing to move that bothers me. Does that sound about right for what you were asking? I hope I understood your question correctly.

{
  "intent": "Determine if the restlessness is localized to the legs and characteristic of restless legs syndrome",
  "question": "Does this uncomfortable urge to move mainly

Oh, um, no, it's not just my legs. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, but it's really my whole body. It's just this... this overall feeling, like a motor running inside me. 

I don't mean to complain, really I don't. It's just that it doesn't seem to stay in one spot. I just feel it everywhere, and I have to get up and do something. Is that... is that helpful? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

```json
{
  "intent": "Assess for chronicity since childhood to distinguish ADHD from adult-onset mood disorders",
  "question": "Has this feeling of having a motor running

Oh, well... yes, I suppose it has been there for a very long time. I hate to even bring it up, because I don't want to sound like I was a bad child or anything. I always tried my best to be good! 

But... well, even back in grade school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright, but maybe a little... careless. I was always losing my papers, or talking out of turn when I shouldn't have been. They were always having to remind me to stay in my seat and finish my work. I just couldn't seem to sit still even then. I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible... I really did try to be a good student. Does that answer what you were asking?
Do these difficulties with focus, staying organized, or finishing tasks continue to cause problems for you at work or at home today?

Oh, well... I really hate to admit this, because I always want to be helpful and do my part, you know? But... yes, it does still cause some problems. I try so hard to keep up with everything, I really do. 

But my family... they've actually had to step in and help me with my bills and paperwork lately. I just get so overwhelmed and things get lost. And... oh, this is so embarrassing to even say... but down at the church and with my community garden group, well, some of the lovely people there have had to redo some of my plans or cover things I volunteered to do but just... forgot about or couldn't finish. 

I just feel awful about it. I hate thinking that these groups I care so much about feel like they can't count on me anymore. I really don't want to be a burden to anyone. I hope you don't think less of me for that... I'm really trying my best to get it all sorted out. Is that the kind of thing you needed to know?
Have you ever had periods lasting several days where you felt unusually energized and needed very little sleep without feeling tired?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I try to get my rest, you know? I don't want to be running around keeping anyone else awake or anything like that. 

I do have trouble sleeping sometimes, but it's more just... tossing and turning because I can't get my brain to quiet down. But I definitely feel tired the next day. I'm not one of those people who can just go and go without sleep, I promise. I try to stick to a good schedule, just like they say you're supposed to. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right for you.

Oh, my heart racing? Well... no, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, maybe a little flutter if I get startled, but nothing out of the ordinary, I don't think. 

I try to take good care of my health, you know? I wouldn't want to ignore something important like my heart. But no, it's mostly just that restless feeling and the trouble sleeping, like I mentioned. My heart seems to be ticking along just fine. I hope that's a good thing? I certainly don't want to add any new problems to the list!

I don't mean to be rude, I promise! It's just... well, especially when I'm at my committee meetings for the garden group or the church... someone will be talking, and a thought will just pop right into my head. And if I don't say it right then and there, I just know I'll lose it completely. So I end up blurting it out before they're finished. 

I always apologize right away, of course. I feel just terrible when I realize I've talked over someone. I really do try to wait my turn, but it just slips out. I hope you don't think I'm a rude person... I'm really trying to work on it. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
